leah: Filing this as a blocker for monarch-v2 bring-up. We see extractive QA span offsets and some translation alignment regressions on vertical zh-Hant / mixed ruby samples after quantizing to q5-int8. F1 dropped 78.4 -> 64.1 on our SQuAD-like vertical subset. Also noticed Hebrew/Arabic parentheses appear on wrong side after detok in some samples. Any ideas?

 tom: Oof. Which tokenizer and normalizer flags did you use for the onboard run? And which quant pipeline (q5-int8) exact repo/commit?

 leah: Onboard command: `python tools/onboard_and_eval.py --model monarch-v2 --evalsets qa-vertical-zh-hant,mt-rtl --tok-profile tok_v3 --quant q5-int8 --seed 42`. Tokenizer repo ref: tok-repo@tok-merge-502. Runtime quant kernels: q5-kern-210. Normalizer config snippet: `preserve_nbsp: false`, `collapse_ideospace: true`, `zwj_adjacent_merge: auto`.

 rachel: If collapse_ideospace is true we might be dropping U+3000 or converting sequences which will shift character offsets used by the QA span reconstructor. Are you seeing token id changes or only detok differences?

 leah: The raw token ids are identical between float16 and q5 runs for the short sample, but the detok step produces a single merged ideographic span in q5 which moves the character offsets. Example (minimal):
```
input: "\n"  # (representing ideographic space + furigana marker in real sample)
fp16 tokens: ["市","　","語","ア","イ"]
q5 tokens:   ["市　語アイ"]  # detok collapsed into single span, offsets shifted
```
This means our answer extractor (which maps token spans back to character offsets) returns wrong substrings.

yuto: Also saw an intermittent long-context kv-ordering difference in q5-kern-210 that changes past-key ordering for >8k contexts; that can cause different attention patterns and slightly different token choices for boundary tokens which makes detok diffs worse. I filed a small test (kern-kv-rtm) that reproduces KV shuffle on synthetic long-prefix sequences.

 infra-bot: deploy:monarch-v2 canary started (canary-id=cny-20260502-4). Monitor link: https://console.redwood/infra/canaries/cny-20260502-4

 tom: Two separate problems: (A) tokenizer/normalizer default changes collapsing ideographic spaces (tok-merge-502) causing deterministic detok shifts; (B) q5 kernel reordering for long-kv windows (q5-kern-210) introducing non-determinism/ordering diffs. Could be compounding.

 leah: Agreed. Immediate mitigation plan I propose: set `collapse_ideospace=false` for vertical-mode in the tokenizer config and pin q5 kernels to q5-kern-208 in canary until we fix ordering. I'll draft a PR and include regression tests for both: - QA offset roundtrip test (vertical zh-hant + ruby) - RTL bracket pairing test (Hebrew + parentheses) - long-kv synthetic test asserting identical past-key ordering across kernels.

 rachel: For the QA offset test please include exact character-level gold spans and the token->char mapping dump. We need example-level F1, EM, and token-diff counts in the PR. Also include a tiny chrF/bleu check for the mt-rtl set so we catch side-effects on translation.

 yuto: I'll bisect tok-repo: tok-merge-502 was the culprit for the ideospace default flip. Reverting that flag locally fixes character offsets and restores F1 from 64.1 -> 78.0 on the vertical QA subset. For the q5 kernel I can reproduce the KV-order shuffle and will push a patch to q5-kern-211 to make write-order stable.

 leah: Pushed failing samples and the eval summary to ML-912: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/ML-912 (includes failing QA examples, token-to-char maps, and the long-kv reproducer).

 infra-bot: infra:ci reported q5-kern-210 failing determinism test in job `kern-determinism/long-kv` (job-id=89321).

 tom: OK assign: @yuto on q5 kernel patch, @leah + @rachel on tokenizer PR to revert ideospace collapse in vertical mode, and I'll coordinate canary pin/rollback with infra. Add perf smoke (latency + token throughputs) to ensure the pin doesn't regress cost.

 yuto: ETA for kernel patch: EOD. I'll also run the q5 regression harness with the patched kernel and report sacreBLEU + SQuAD-F1 diffs here.

 leah: Thanks. Small note: when adding the QA unit test please include both byte-offset and unicode codepoint offsets in the mapping (we use codepoint offsets for most consumers).

 rachel: :+1: Also include an explicit test where NBSPs (U+00A0) interact with U+3000 ideographic space; we've seen weird merges when both present.

 leah: Will do. Will update ML-912 and post PR link here when ready. If canary shows more visible regressions we should rollback cny-20260502-4.

 infra-bot: monitor: canary health is being tracked. Alert threshold set to 5% delta on EM or 10% on sacreBLEU for these eval groups.

 leah: Appreciate the quick triage everyone. Bisect + pin path gives us a short-term rollback while fixes go in. I'll post the PR numbers in ML-912.
